brief: Raymond James keeps an upward equity bias into year-end on seasonal strength and improving fundamentals, but flags weak internals beneath the surface: about 74% of S&P 500 constituents are down more than 10% from their 52-week highs even as the cap-weighted index sits just 0.5% below its own all-time high, with mega-caps masking the average stock's weakness. Base case is sideways consolidation and rotation, not a broader pullback; a stabilization in rates could pull capital out of mega-cap growth and high-beta names and back into pressured areas, which the firm would read as healthy broadening rather than a top. It is watching whether small-caps and the equal-weight S&P hold their 200-day moving averages, calling a break below both a signal of deteriorating breadth that raises pullback risk. On rates, a hotter September core CPI print pushed yields up, but RSI and a bearish MACD cross suggest yield momentum is waning, with the 20-day moving average the next inflection test. Consensus sees about 28% y/y Q3 EPS growth led by Energy and Technology, a high bar after last quarter's 26% beat; guidance and the market's reaction to results, not the beat itself, will matter most.
